dedupe_keys.name: economic benefits of resilient pnt in the uk london economics concept paper october 2022

description: This concept paper by London Economics for the Royal Institute of Navigation's UK PNT Leadership Seminar tests the hypothesis that the UK can generate value and sustainable leadership by investing in resilient position, navigation and timing (PNT). It notes that GNSS underpins much of the modern economy through global availability and zero cost, but growing reliance exposes weaknesses as attacks on PNT systems become larger and more sophisticated. The paper recalls the earlier estimate that a five-day GNSS loss would cost the UK about GBP 5.2 billion, with road, maritime and emergency and justice services accounting for 67 percent of impacts, and sizes the market for resilient PNT products and services, reporting a UK market of about GBP 1 billion a year with a further GBP 10 billion of market potential and scenarios where the UK captures up to a 4 percent share of an enlarged market. Producer: London Economics with guidance from the RIN Resilient PNT Advisory Group; published in October 2022 and hosted by UK Space. Coverage: the United Kingdom. Access: a free PDF. Licence and cost: free; no licence found in the pages read. Caveats: a concept paper with high-level assumptions, market estimates, not measured outcomes, and figures quoted from earlier studies. Simulation uses: it supplies economic loss and benefit parameters for GNSS-disruption scenarios and investment appraisal. Related records: the UK GNSS disruption economic impact study (case_study-uk-gnss-disruption-economic-impact) and the Blackett review (case_study-uk-blackett-review-gnss-dependencies-2018).
